title: Claude Code vs Codex vs Gemini CLI (October 2026) · DejaViewed
h1: Claude Code vs Codex vs Gemini CLI
crumb: Claude Code vs Codex vs Gemini CLI
description: Claude Code vs Codex vs Gemini CLI, verified Oct 22 2026: prices, free tiers, models, hooks, skills, MCP, and what creators actually use each one for.
answer: As of 22 October 2026, Claude Code has the deepest agent harness and the most creator workflows built on it, but it starts at $20 a month, while Codex is the only one of the three you can start free and its CLI is open source. Gemini CLI stopped serving free personal Google accounts on 18 June 2026 [[s:g-blog]], so it now fits only teams that already pay for Gemini Code Assist or a Gemini API key.

list: **Gemini CLI's free tier is gone.** Google announced on 19 May 2026 that Gemini CLI would stop serving free individual accounts and Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers on 18 June 2026 [[s:g-blog]]. The repo README now says Gemini CLI "was replaced by Antigravity CLI" for those users [[s:gem-repo]]. The repo's own quota page still lists the old 1,000 requests a day, which is out of date [[s:gem-quota-doc]].
**Antigravity CLI is the free Google option now.** Its individual plan is $0 with "basic weekly rate limits", and Google does not publish the size of those limits [[s:antigravity-pricing]].

**Claude's June 15 billing split was paused.** A creator reported that `claude -p` and Agent SDK usage would move to per-token billing ([[e:DYXWNTERFhZ]]). Anthropic's support article says the change was paused and that this usage still counts against plan limits [[s:cc-sdk-billing]].
**Max and Team plans gained monthly API credits on 7 October 2026.** Max 5x gets $100 and Max 20x $200, and the credits do not cover interactive Claude Code [[s:cc-credits]].
**Codex retired GPT-5.5 for ChatGPT sign-in on 14 October 2026** and now recommends GPT-6.1 Sol [[s:codex-models]].

sections.h2: What creators actually use each one for

corpus.lead: We counted every saved post in the DejaViewed corpus that names each tool, then sorted those posts by what the creator was doing. {union} entries name at least one of the three. Counts are computed from the live catalog each time this page is built.
corpus.method: Method: a tool counts when it is named anywhere in an entry, including its caption and transcript. A theme counts when it appears in the entry's title, summary, tags, tools or takeaways. One entry can count toward several tools and themes. Tiers are our S/A/B/C quality ratings.

themes.label: Automation and agents that run a business

groups.label: [[t:gemini-cli|Gemini CLI]]
groups.note: The corpus barely covers Gemini CLI. The main entry is a 2025 post about the free tier that Google has since ended.

paras: **Claude Code** posts are mostly about extending the harness rather than raw coding. Boris Cherny's team tips ([[e:DVQ5o6YDfsp]]) and his CLAUDE.md ([[e:DV6QY8QjoRW]]) set the plan-first pattern, and roundups like [[e:DUzg0n1jRK-]] list the skill packs people install. A second cluster is about stretching usage limits: rerouting the harness through OpenRouter ([[e:DW6yhr6CHoP]]) or letting the top model plan while cheaper subagents execute ([[e:Da1hOm7scjR]]).

**Codex** shows up most as a second opinion on Claude's work. Creators run it as an auditor of Claude Code output ([[e:DV3lILoEfzS]]), cross-audit plans between the two models ([[e:DeW79CbCkO3]]), or call it from inside Claude Code with OpenAI's plugin ([[e:DaojVuSNKno]]). Solo builds lean on its scheduled tasks ([[e:DdDT0X0KC64]]) and its hands-off asset work, such as a Blender model built and embedded with Three.js ([[e:DdUyTAAJTj6]]). One tier list ranks Codex and Claude Code level and calls Codex cheaper for comparable output ([[e:DX7oRT3J1Hq]]).

**Gemini CLI** has one strong entry, and it is now historical: a post about the free 1,000-requests-a-day tier ([[e:DLuiACnKWP9]]). Creators who wanted a free terminal agent have looked at Kimi Code CLI ([[e:MoonshotAI/kimi-cli]]), and one agency stack pairs Claude Code with Google Antigravity ([[e:DUODsbFkTC3]]).

Several creators run two of these side by side. One builds a dashboard that drives both Claude Code and Codex subscriptions from one screen ([[e:DZErwKSCT2z]]), and a trending reverse-engineering repo works with either ([[e:DeV2n53gLgf]]).

rows: You already pay for Claude Pro or Max, you want the richest set of hooks, skills and plugins (see our [best Claude Code skills and plugins](/best/claude-code-skills-and-plugins)), and you want a 1M-token context by default.
You want to start free on ChatGPT Free or $8 Go, you want an Apache-2.0 CLI you can read and fork, or you want a second model to audit what Claude writes.
Your company already has a Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise license or Vertex billing. Individuals on a personal Google account are pointed to Antigravity CLI instead.
You plan with one model and audit with the other. Claude Code plus Codex is the pairing the corpus shows most, through OpenAI's Codex plugin for Claude Code.

paras: All three now share the same building blocks: hooks, Agent Skills, plugins or extensions, MCP, subagents and a headless mode. The differences that matter are price of entry, license, and which ecosystem your team already lives in. We did not run our own benchmark, so this page does not rank code quality.

unverified: Codex context window size per model: the Codex docs do not state it.
Numeric limits of the ChatGPT Free plan for Codex: OpenAI does not publish them.
Antigravity CLI's license and the size of its free weekly limits: Google's pages do not state them.
The old Gemini CLI figure of 60 requests a minute on Gemini 2.5 Pro: only third-party pages carry it now.
Code quality: our corpus records what creators did with each tool, not a controlled same-task test.
